claims.claim: D&D Beyond's own launch article says the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide's handouts serve as a template for building settlements.
claims.source: Mike Bernier, 'What's New in the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide?', D&D Beyond, 12 Nov 2024
claims.quote: creating NPCs and building settlements
claims.routeHint: curl with browser user agent; note the page uses non-breaking spaces, so longer quotations will not match on a naive search

claims.claim: Wizards of the Coast states that the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide replaces all rules in the 2014 version of the book.
claims.source: DND Staff, 'Updates in the Dungeon Master's Guide (2024)', D&D Beyond, 20 Feb 2025
claims.quote: it replaces all rules in the 2014 version of the book

claims.claim: In the publisher's own chapter list the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide puts campaign-setting creation in chapter 5, not in the adventure-environment chapter the 2014 book used.
claims.source: DND Staff, 'Updates in the Dungeon Master's Guide (2024)', D&D Beyond, 20 Feb 2025
claims.quote: explores how to create a campaign and campaign setting
claims.confidence: medium — the page asserts the 2024 placement; the contrast with 2014 is my framing, and the page does not name the 2014 chapter

claims.claim: An official free D&D Beyond encounter opens a settlement entry with the settlement's name, a population figure, and its people's trade, in one sentence.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: Icehaven is a village of 5,000 souls

claims.claim: The same official column calls Icehaven a village while giving it a population of 5,000, a figure the publisher's own 2024 settlement handout places in the town band.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: Icehaven is a village of 5,000 souls
claims.confidence: medium — the mismatch is a comparison across two WotC documents of different years, not a statement either page makes

claims.claim: The same column names a settlement's leader as office title plus given name plus surname, in that order.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: The leader of the village, Starosta Ernath Noack

claims.claim: The official column cues its read-aloud with an instruction that licenses paraphrase rather than verbatim reading.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: read or paraphrase the following

claims.claim: The arrival read-aloud describes the village through its housing stock and street pattern rather than through its inhabitants.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: mostly made up of steep-roofed cottages, separated by twisting streets

claims.claim: The column then lists the settlement's important locations by name and numbers them as labelled sub-entries.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: The following areas in Icehaven are important to this encounter

claims.claim: The column expresses a settlement's market depth as a gp threshold above which a specialty shop must be searched for, the same economic handle the 2024 settlement handout records.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: an item that costs more than 100 gp
claims.confidence: medium — the equation with the 2024 handout's field is my comparison, not the page's

claims.claim: A second official column names a governing officer as an invented office title plus given name plus surname, followed by the plain English office in apposition.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Battle of the Braggarts', 2020
claims.quote: Taskhand Durth Mirimm, the current governor
claims.page: 'The Wastes of Xhorhas and the City of Jigow'

claims.claim: The same column qualifies its own size label, calling Jigow a small city by population while describing its extent as a sprawl of towns.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Battle of the Braggarts', 2020
claims.quote: Jigow is a small city by population, but its sprawl of towns
claims.page: 'The Wastes of Xhorhas and the City of Jigow'

claims.claim: The same column ties each read-aloud to the precise moment and threshold at which it is spoken.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Battle of the Braggarts', 2020
claims.quote: Read or paraphrase the following as the characters enter the Wartpimple Tavern

claims.claim: An official D&D Beyond column states that describing travel in an interesting and engaging way is hard to do.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Trek to Ten-Towns', 2020
claims.quote: Describing travel in an interesting and engaging way is hard to do

claims.claim: The same column advises compressing an unremarkable stretch into a single sentence rather than accumulating uninspired description.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Trek to Ten-Towns', 2020
claims.quote: better to simply describe the day’s travel in a single sentence

claims.claim: The same column tells the DM to vary the wording of a repeated transition so the read-aloud does not sound scripted.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Trek to Ten-Towns', 2020
claims.quote: so it doesn't seem like you're reading from a script

claims.claim: A reporter covering the publisher's own preview says Settlements is one of the alphabetically arranged topics in the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide's DM's Toolbox chapter.
claims.source: Randy, Gaming Nexus, reporting a Wizards of the Coast preview interview with Chris Perkins and Todd Kenreck, 10 Oct 2024
claims.quote: The topics are so varied that they've resorted to an alphabetical presentation
claims.routeHint: curl with browser user agent; 'Settlements' appears in the bulleted topic list further down the page
claims.confidence: medium — the quotation supports the alphabetical arrangement; the presence of Settlements rests on a one-word list item on the same page

claims.claim: The same report says the 2024 settlement generator's first roll produces the town's defining feature, giving a Sprawling Cemetery in the demonstration.
claims.source: Randy, Gaming Nexus, reporting a Wizards of the Coast preview with Chris Perkins, 10 Oct 2024
claims.quote: the town's defining feature is [roll the dice] a Sprawling Cemetery

claims.claim: The same report gives the current-calamity roll's demonstration result as monsters infesting the settlement.
claims.source: Randy, Gaming Nexus, reporting a Wizards of the Coast preview with Chris Perkins, 10 Oct 2024
claims.quote: What current calamity is befalling the town: Monsters infest the settlement

claims.claim: The same report shows the leadership roll returning a political condition rather than a person, an illegitimate leader causing civil unrest.
claims.source: Randy, Gaming Nexus, reporting a Wizards of the Coast preview with Chris Perkins, 10 Oct 2024
claims.quote: Local leaders: An illegitimate leader causing civil unrest

claims.claim: The same report says the 2024 settlement tables are rolled live, with a designer building a random settlement on the spot.
claims.source: Randy, Gaming Nexus, reporting a Wizards of the Coast preview with Chris Perkins, 10 Oct 2024
claims.quote: Chris Perkins builds a random settlement while he's just sitting there

claims.claim: A long-standing D&D usability critic judges the 2014 Dungeon Master's Guide's organization not the best way to parse the job of being a dungeon master.
claims.source: Mike Shea (Sly Flourish), 'Gems of the D&D Dungeon Master's Guide', 1 Mar 2021
claims.quote: the best way to parse the job of being a dungeon master
claims.page: 'How to Read the Dungeon Master's Guide'

claims.claim: The freely licensed System Reference Document 5.2.1 contains no settlement-description rules: its four occurrences of settlement are all inside spell and equipment text.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, System Reference Document 5.2.1 (CC-BY-4.0), 2025
claims.page: whole document; grep over extracted text
claims.routeHint: direct PDF fetch, pdftotext, grep -c -i settlement returns 4, all in Commune with Nature, spellcasting services and crafting text

claims.claim: Neither freely licensed SRD, 5.1 nor 5.2.1, mentions read-aloud or boxed text anywhere, so no lawful open-licence source carries the form.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, System Reference Document 5.1 (2016) and 5.2.1 (2025)
claims.page: whole documents; grep over extracted text
claims.routeHint: direct PDF fetch of both, pdftotext, grep -i for 'read aloud', 'read-aloud', 'boxed text' returns zero hits in each
